claims.text:
Brego means "chief, leader, king, lord" in Old English, which Tolkien used to represent Rohanese in his works.
Outside The Lord of the Rings, the plural form of the word, Bregan ("Rulers") also appeared in earlier writings as one of the Old English words for the Valar by Ælfwine.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "III. The Quenta: Appendix 1: Fragments of a translation of The Quenta Noldorinwa into Old English, made by Ælfwine or Eriol; together with Old English equivalents of Elvish names"

claims.text: Brego became King at the death of his father Eorl the Young in . During his rule the migration of the Éothéod to Calenardhon continued, and Brego defended the borders of Rohan against their enemies (the Dunlendings and Easterlings) and drove off the Wold the remaining Orcs and Balchoth.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age"

claims.text: Brego built the Golden Hall of Meduseld (), and made Edoras the capital of Rohan.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age"

claims.text: His eldest son Baldor in his pride went into the Paths of the Dead never to be found again, and Brego died of grief the next year. He was followed by his second son, Aldor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The House of Eorl", "The Kings of the Mark"
